Cluster samples using ConSpec component scores

Source: R/spec_clust.R
spec_clust.Rd

Performs k-means clustering on component scores obtained from a ConSpec analysis, such as contrastive PCA or contrastive CCA. If reference labels are supplied, the adjusted Rand index (ARI) is also calculated.

spec_clust(
  score_mat,
  k = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  components = NULL,
  nstart = 25,
  iter.max = 100,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

score_mat

A numeric matrix or data frame containing component scores, with samples in rows and components in columns.

k

Number of clusters. If NULL and group is supplied, k is set to the number of unique non-missing reference labels.

group

Optional vector of reference group labels. Must have one value per row of score_mat.

components

Integer vector specifying the score dimensions used for clustering. By default, all columns of score_mat are used.

nstart

Number of random initializations passed to stats::kmeans(). Default is 25.

iter.max

Maximum number of k-means iterations.

seed

Optional random seed for reproducibility.

...

Additional arguments passed to stats::kmeans().

Value

A list containing:

cluster

Integer vector of cluster assignments.

ari

Adjusted Rand index, or NULL if group is not supplied.

kmeans

The fitted object returned by stats::kmeans().

scores

The score matrix used for clustering.

components

The component indices used for clustering.

Examples

set.seed(1)
scores <- matrix(rnorm(100), nrow = 20)

# Unsupervised clustering
fit <- spec_clust(scores, k = 2)
fit$cluster
#>  [1] 1 1 2 1 2 2 2 1 2 1 1 2 2 2 2 2 1 1 1 1

# Clustering evaluation using known labels
group <- rep(c("A", "B"), each = 10)
fit <- spec_clust(scores, k = 2, group = group)
fit$ari
#> [1] -0.05555556
